summary: Alberta's register dates the steel tower to 2017; 1946-48 government annual reports describe an earlier tower on the site being replaced.

events.note: Material taken to the Whitecourt Lookout Tower site to replace an old tower becoming unsafe; road, culverts and a well built (annual report year ended 31 March 1947, quoted by Canada Lookouts)
Tower replaced by a new one on the same site (annual report year ended 31 March 1948, quoted by Canada Lookouts)
Tower road improved and maintained (annual report year ended 31 March 1949, quoted by Canada Lookouts)
Register construction year for the present steel tower

evidence.supports: steel tower, 30 m tall, 1,172 m elevation, in the register record for Whitecourt
register gives 2017 as the construction year
register lists the tower as active and reached by road
1946 material taken to replace an old tower becoming unsafe
evidence.quote: Material was obtained and transported to the Whitecourt Lookout Tower site to replace the old tower, as this is becoming unsafe.

evidence.supports: road cleared and graded, nine culverts built along it
evidence.quote: The Whitecourt Lookout Tower road was cleared for 3,850 yards and graded for 3,192 yards, also nine culverts were constructed on this road.

evidence.supports: well dug and cribbed at the tower site
evidence.quote: A well was also dug and cribbed at this tower site.

evidence.supports: report for year ended 31 March 1948: tower replaced by a new one on the same site
evidence.quote: Whitecourt Tower: This tower was replaced by a new one on the same site.

evidence.supports: following year's report: tower road improved and maintained
evidence.quote: The Whitecourt tower road was improved and maintained.

evidence.supports: lookouts are an integral component of detection and sited where visibility is favourable
evidence.quote: Fire lookouts are an integral component of wildfire detection in Alberta and are located where visibility is favourable to detect and report wildfires.

notes_for_editor: Brief's access 'closed' is not stated by any source read, so no access level is recorded; visit.drive_up comes from the register's ACCESS_MODE 'drive'. Agency is left out: the brief's 'Alberta Wildfire' is not named in any source read for this site, and the 1946-48 reports name the Department of Lands and Mines. The 1946-48 entries are read through a lookout-history site that quotes the annual reports; the originals were not read. No source says whether the 1947 tower stood where the 2017 steel tower now stands, so the story does not say it did. The Whitecourt Star 2013 article is about the Pass Creek lookout and was not used. The story gives Alberta only; no source read ties the site to the town of Whitecourt.
